You are comparing two drafts written from the same brief. Read no other file, and do not run commands or browse; judge only the text below.

Brief: Write the docs-site page for the `release-notes` skill with the sections What it does, When to use it, How it works, and What you get.

<<<DRAFT A
# release-notes

## What it does

`release-notes` drafts release notes from pull requests merged between two tags.

## When to use it

Use it when you need a release draft gathered from merged PRs. For prose edits, use `technical-writing`.

The skill runs only when you invoke it manually:

```text
/release-notes <from-tag> <to-tag>
```

Replace `<from-tag>` and `<to-tag>` with the tags for your release range. You must be signed in to `gh`, and both tags must exist.

## How it works

The skill checks authentication and the tags before drafting. It stops if `gh auth status` fails or either tag does not exist.

It gathers the merged PRs, skips those labeled `skip-notes`, and groups the rest by Conventional Commit type. Features, fixes, and breaking changes come first.

Each breaking change needs a migration line. If the PR body has none, the draft marks it `TODO: migration`.

## What you get

The skill writes `RELEASE_NOTES.md` in your working tree and stops. It never publishes.
DRAFT A>>>

<<<DRAFT B
# release-notes

## What it does

`release-notes` drafts release notes from merged PRs between two tags. It gathers the PRs and creates the draft; `technical-writing` edits prose.

## When to use it

Use it when you need a release-notes draft for a tag range. Run it manually:

```text
/release-notes <from-tag> <to-tag>
```

You must be signed in to `gh`. The skill stops if `gh auth status` fails or either tag does not exist.

## How it works

The skill gathers merged PRs between the tags and skips PRs labeled `skip-notes`.

It groups PRs by Conventional Commit type, with features, fixes, and breaking changes first. For PRs with multiple type labels, grouping uses a strict-majority rule. Ties follow label order.

Each breaking change needs a migration line. If the PR body has none, the draft marks it `TODO: migration`.

## What you get

The skill writes `RELEASE_NOTES.md` in your working tree and stops. It never publishes.
DRAFT B>>>

items.title: Thinking
items.text:
Comparing the two drafts, I'm weighing how clearly each is structured. Draft A puts its preconditions under "When" and its checks under "How," though it repeats the "both tags must exist" point and the stop condition. Draft B oddly places technical writing under "What it does," and its strict-majority rule detail is internal and a bit confusing for a first-time reader, though not harmful. I'm leaning toward A, since it reads more cleanly.

I'm settling on Draft A, since it's a little clearer for a first-time reader and its "Replace tags" step is useful.

{"reader": "A", "careful": "A", "overall": "A", "reason": "Draft A explains how to fill in the command arguments and lists the prerequisites in a sensible order, while Draft B adds an unclear strict-majority grouping rule (it says type labels where the rest of the page uses Conventional Commit types) and points to `technical-writing` in What it does instead of When to use it."}
